Metadata of an output

Source: R/output.R
pub_meta.Rd

Outputs are ordinary R objects (data.frames, ggplots, texts, ...). pubflow can attach extra information to them, e.g. a caption or an id, called metadata.

Usage

pub_meta(x, key = NULL)

pub_set_meta(x, ...)

pub_meta(x) <- value

Arguments

x

An R object (not NULL).

key

character(1) name of an entry or NULL for the whole list.

...

Named entries to set; NULL removes an entry.

value

Named list of metadata (or NULL to remove all).

Value

  • pub_meta(): the named list of metadata (empty if there is none) or the entry key (NULL if absent).

  • pub_set_meta(): x with the new metadata.

  • pub_meta<-: x with the new metadata.

Details

Functions

  • pub_meta() reads the metadata;

  • pub_set_meta() sets or removes single entries;

  • pub_meta<- replaces all of it.

Functions such as pub_table() and pub_figure() set metadata for you; use these functions to read or change it afterwards.

Keys

KeyApplies toMeaning
titleany itemheading above the item
captiontable, figurenumbered caption ("Table 1: ..."); "" for none
idtable, figurename for cross-references (see pub_text())
width, heightfiguresize in inches (default 8 x 6)
out_widthfigurewidth relative to the text width, e.g. "90%"
font_sizetablefont size in pt
landscapetable, figureplace on landscape pages (DOCX, PDF)
lockedtable, figurelock in DOCX against accidental edits
fallbackwidgetstatic figure shown where HTML is not available
stampfigureset when a step returns a plot, not a rendered one

An id must be unique in a document. It starts with a letter, ends with a letter or digit and has only letters, digits, _ and - in between, e.g. "slopes-1".

You can also add keys of your own. pubflow keeps them but does not use them.

Huxtables

The caption of a huxtable lives in huxtable's own caption (huxtable::caption()), and pub_meta() and friends read and write it there. Subsetting with [ and cbind() keep this caption but drop all other metadata. So set the metadata on the final table.

See also

pub_type(), pub_figure(), pub_text(), pub_table()

Examples

x <- pub_set_meta(data.frame(a = 1:2), title = "Raw data", locked = TRUE)
pub_meta(x)
#> $title
#> [1] "Raw data"
#> 
#> $locked
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
pub_meta(x, "title")
#> [1] "Raw data"

x <- pub_set_meta(x, locked = NULL)
names(pub_meta(x))
#> [1] "title"

pub_meta(x) <- list(title = "Data")
pub_meta(x)
#> $title
#> [1] "Data"
#> 

# the target of the cross-reference `@tab:slopes` in a text
tab <- pub_table(data.frame(a = 1:2), caption = "Slopes")
tab <- pub_set_meta(tab, id = "slopes")
pub_meta(tab, "id")
#> [1] "slopes"
